Acyclovir is an effective medication for treating herpes simplex and herpes zoster infections. It reduces contagious lesions on skin and mucous membranes, including those caused by genital herpes. With antiviral properties that inhibit viral spread, acyclovir helps control symptoms effectively. The recommended dosage varies based on the condition; typically 200 mg for skin and mucosal herpes over five days, or 400 mg for shingles lasting ten days. It’s also used in AIDS and HIV treatment but is not advised for children under one year old, pregnant women, or those with kidney issues or allergies to its components. Common side effects include headaches, nausea, and allergic reactions. Store acyclovir in a dry, dark place.

If you’re looking for reliable information on common over‑the‑counter pain relievers, remember that acetaminophen and ibuprofen are the most frequently used. Acetaminophen is generally safe when taken under the recommended dose of 4 g per day, but exceeding this can damage the liver. Ibuprofen, a nonsteroidal anti‑inflammatory drug (NSAID), helps reduce inflammation and pain; however, it may irritate the stomach lining or increase blood pressure if used long term.
